5.0.0.en: Wherever Christ moved, the crowds followed Him because of His moving teachings and His care for them in healing their diseases and freeing them from demons.

5.0.1.en: On this day He came to the lake of Gennesaret, whose meaning is "garden of delight," which is sometimes called the Sea of Galilee or the Sea of Tiberias.

5.1.0.en: It was morning, at the beginning of the day, when the fishermen had returned with their boats from fishing at night, and had washed their nets of the clinging weeds in preparation for fishing at sundown, and were about to go to their homes to rest.

5.2.0.en: There were two boats, one belonging to Simon and his brother Andrew, and the other to James and John the sons of Zebedee. Christ entered the boat of Simon Peter and asked him to thrust out a little from the land, where the crowds were pressing, and He stood teaching from the boat His moving spiritual teachings. Simon had known Him before and Christ had visited his house, but he had not yet left everything and followed Him.

5.2.1.en: God may come to you and call you to prayer, or to reading His Holy Book, or to doing some good and serving others at a time you do not expect or when you want to rest; so do not refuse, that you may enjoy God's abundant graces.

5.3.0.en: Simon and his brother Andrew were grieved because they had caught no fish that night, and consequently were in need of food for that day. After they heard Christ's teachings, their hearts were at rest, but Christ would not forget their material need, so He asked them to put the boat out into the deep of the sea.

5.3.1.en: If you give time to worship and service, be confident that God solves your material problems. Hold fast to Him and rely on Him and go deeper in knowing Him.

5.4.0.en: Christ's command was strange to Simon for two reasons:

5.4.1.en: (1) He had toiled all night and found no fish in the sea in the places he knew from his experience, and at the proper time for fishing, which is night.

5.4.2.en: (2) By experience in fishing, in the deep one does not catch with nets but with a hook some of the fish that are found on the bottom.

5.4.3.en: But his being moved by Christ's miracles and teachings made him obey Him more than his own mind and experience. May obedience rise above your mind and your feelings, for the word of God in the Holy Bible and the Church is more important than anything, so you obey it despite how hard it is for you.

5.5.0.en: When Simon obeyed, he was surprised that the net filled with a great many fish that he had not expected, and as the net was about to break because of the abundance of fish, they unloaded some of them from it into the boat, and it filled. And they called to their partners James and John, who came with their boat and filled it also. The two boats were almost sinking because of the abundance of fish, and they also drew in the net with the fish remaining in it, and with difficulty reached the shore with their great catch. Your toil alone without Christ does not benefit you, but if you obey Him in your spiritual striving, be confident of His abundant, unexpected blessing that satisfies the spirit and the body (the two boats). And if you achieve great success, thank God, the One to whom credit is due, throughout your life.

5.6.0.en: All that were with him: that is, Andrew and the hired men who helped him in fishing.

5.6.1.en: Before the power of Christ and His divinity, evident in His command to the fish and their obeying Him contrary to the laws of nature, Simon felt his weakness and sins, so he bowed down before Christ, declaring his unworthiness to have Him in his boat, and said to Him, "Depart from me," since he felt that His place is glory in heaven, and not being on earth in a lowly boat like this one.

5.6.2.en: Do God's benefactions lead you to thank Him, to humble yourself before Him and to repent of your sins?

5.7.0.en: The same awe came upon the sons of Zebedee, who were in the boat accompanying the boat of Simon and Andrew. And since Simon had qualified through obedience, repentance and confession of Christ's power, he deserved to be called by Christ to discipleship under His hands so as to serve souls. For these are the qualifications of service.

5.8.0.en: It seems that the first call of Simon and some disciples, mentioned in Jn 1:35-42), made them follow Christ at times, then return to their work, which was fishing, at other times. Christ may have allowed them to toil and catch nothing, so that they might know their weakness and their need of Him, and at the same time He worked the miracle of the great catch of fish so that they might be reassured of the ease of providing for their material needs if they followed Him.

5.8.1.en: In any case, after the call was confirmed here a second time, in which He called not only Simon but also Andrew and James and John the sons of Zebedee, as is shown by the words "they followed him," then they forsook all with faith and new obedience, and even rejoiced.

5.8.2.en: God is longsuffering with you until you trust in Him and follow Him and enjoy His blessings and His service. So do not let your material attachments, projects and responsibilities hinder you from serving God, for nothing in the world equals it. It is a clear test of the extent of your love for Him: is it more than for the world?

5.9.0.en: Leprosy (similar to what is now leprosy and vitiligo) was a contagious disease, and signifies uncleanness because it results from sin. Whoever was afflicted with it, according to the Law of Moses, was isolated outside the community and no one touched him lest he be defiled. But when this leper heard of Christ and His healing of disease, he believed and pushed through the crowds, although the leprosy, as Luke the physician states, was spread over his body, and he bowed humbly before Him and asked Christ with gentleness ("if thou wilt") and faith ("thou canst") to cleanse him.

5.10.0.en: Christ could have healed him with a word, but He touched him to show His divinity in His authority over disease and His tenderness toward the leper. At the same time He is not against the Law, for He sent him to the priest to fulfill the Law.

5.11.0.en: Offer for thy cleansing: the Law required the leper to present a sacrifice as a declaration of his repentance and his resolve not to return to sin, and as a type of the redemption of Christ, who takes away all our sins. Because Christ does not want display and fame, He told the leper to tell no one, but to fulfill the Law, which required that when a leper was healed, he go to the priest to examine him and make sure of his healing and give him a certificate of it before he mixed with anyone.

5.11.1.en: Here Christ's saying appears that He did not come to destroy but to fulfill the Law (Mt 5:17).

5.11.2.en: But when the crowds heard the news of the leper's healing, they felt that this was the Messiah, because the prophets had prophesied that among His works would be healing precisely this disease because of its difficulty, and so also Christ said in reply to the two disciples of John the Baptist who asked Him whether He was the Messiah, He told them that He cleanses lepers (Lk 7:22-23); so the crowds pressed around Christ seeking healing of their diseases.

5.12.0.en: Despite Christ's concern for healing the sick and serving the crowds, He teaches us not to be so occupied that we neglect prayer and being alone with God in quiet away from people, for this is the spiritual provision that strengthens us so that we can serve others and face the problems of life.

5.12.1.en: If you believe in God's power, which is able to solve your problems, then take refuge in Him with humility and be confident that He will remove all your troubles, and be ready to leave all your sins by repentance, and He will also support you until you are rid of them however hard they are. He loves you and has come for your salvation.

5.13.0.en: Christ entered one of the houses of Capernaum, as we know from the details of this incident mentioned in (Mt 9:2-8, Mk 2:1-12), and among those gathered around Him was a group of Pharisees, that is, the separated ones, who felt that they were the best spiritual class in Jewish society and were characterized by pride; and also a group of teachers of the Law, who were literalists in their adherence to the Law without its essence. They had come from different lands to examine Christ's teachings and judge them, so they were sitting proudly watching Him. A great number of Jews had gathered from the villages of Galilee around Capernaum, and even from the villages of Judea, which lie south of Galilee, and they brought many sick to Him and He healed them, so the people marveled at the power of God in Him.

5.13.1.en: Do you listen with humility to the teachings of the Church, or do you listen in order to judge the preacher with pride?

5.13.2.en: Let every word you hear or book you read be a spiritual message from God for you to apply in your life, and you will find the salvation of your soul.

5.14.0.en: Among the many sick who crowded around Christ, four men (as mentioned in Mt 9) came carrying a paralytic on his bed, and because of the crowd around the door they found no way to reach Christ except by going up onto the roof by the back stairs. There was an opening in the roof which they covered with wood in winter and removed in summer, so they removed these wooden boards that were among the baked bricks (the burnt bricks that cover the roof to prevent rain water from penetrating), and tied the paralytic's bed and let it down through the roof, and he came down before the Lord of glory Jesus.

5.14.1.en: How much great effort these four men spent, which declares their faith in Christ and their love for the sick man! They signify the classes of the Church coming with faith to Christ (bishops, priests, deacons, people) to find salvation in Him; or the four Evangelists, who by their Gospels carry us to faith in Christ. Show your love and faith by practical striving, and you will rejoice the heart of God and receive His blessings.

5.15.0.en: When Christ saw the practical faith of these four friends, He cared greatly for their practical intercession for their friend, so He granted him the forgiveness of his sins, which was the real cause of his illness. For He cuts off the disease from its root and origin, and this confirms His divinity and His authority to forgive sins, for none can do that but God. This does not mean that the paralytic had no faith; rather his inability to move and speak did not give him an opportunity to express his faith, but his accepting, in this bad state of health, to leave his house and enter into the crowd, and that they should take him up to the roof and tie the bed and let him down, bearing this toil and the risk of falling while being let down ... all this confirms his desire for healing and his faith.

5.15.1.en: Your enduring sufferings with contentment confirms your love and faith in God. Intercede through the saints your friends, for this rejoices God's heart and He answers their requests.

5.16.0.en: The scribes and Pharisees were vexed at Christ's words, declaring that the One who forgives sins is God alone, so how does Christ command the forgiveness of sins?

5.17.0.en: Christ knew their thoughts without their speaking them, and none knows the inner thoughts of man but God, so this is a proof of the divinity of Christ, who rebuked them for their doubts.

5.18.0.en: Christ asked the scribes and Pharisees which is easier, forgiving sins or bodily healing? .... Of course bodily healing; for Christ had done the greater, which is the forgiveness of sin, but to answer their doubts and confirm His divinity and authority, He gave healing to the paralytic with one word, to rise up and take up his bed.

5.18.1.en: God's love for you is strong and constant, and you feel it clearly in the Holy Bible, prayer and the holy Mysteries, but He confirms it to you with many gifts, that perhaps you may understand His infinite love for you.

5.19.0.en: The disease left him at once and he recovered his full health, so that he was able to take up his bed and return to his house, and as he made his way through the crowds he was thanking God and praising Him.

5.19.1.en: God's giving to us is generous, beyond what we expect or ask, therefore we ought to thank Him at all times for His gifts, and join with the Church in praising Him.

5.20.0.en: Before this great miracle, everyone marveled and glorified God, who had performed these miracles among them, bewildered at the power of the miracle and the authority of Christ.

5.21.0.en: In the place of tax collection sat Matthew the tax collector, whom Luke the Evangelist calls here by his other name, Levi, as an honor to him, to return him to his first great function, which is service; for the whole tribe of Levi was devoted to the service of the Temple. Christ called him to follow Him, so he left his job with all the material gains connected with it and his great position, and followed Christ, preferring spiritual gain to material.

5.21.1.en: In order to free time for God, you will be compelled to give up some of your comfort, your preoccupations and your material gains. Is Christ in your eyes worth this?

5.22.0.en: Since Levi (Matthew) rejoiced in following Christ, he also thought of his fellow tax collectors and his sinner friends, whom Luke here refers to as "others," and how to draw them to follow Christ. So he made a feast in his house in which he gathered all these, and invited Christ to it, confident that His teachings would surely affect them and lead them to repentance. Do you feel your responsibility toward the members of your family, your friends, your neighbors and your colleagues at work? How do you try to draw them to the love of God and attachment to Him?

5.23.0.en: The Pharisees and scribes, who were the spiritual leaders of the Jews, were vexed at Christ's mixing with sinners and said so. But because of their embarrassment to say this to Christ, they said it to His disciples, thinking only of their own appearance and people's opinion of them and not the salvation of others.

5.23.1.en: Bear the opinion of opposing people if the weak and despised need your service, as long as your aim is to offer Christ's love to all.

5.24.0.en: Christ made clear here that sin is weakness and sickness, so sinners need us to have compassion on them and treat them, and not to keep away from them. He is the true Physician who came into the world to heal all who have fallen into the sickness of sin.

5.24.1.en: But those who think in their pride that they are healthy or righteous, these have no benefit from Christ's teachings unless they first repent of their self-righteousness, and this may come if they fall into a severe temptation.

5.24.2.en: Have compassion on sinners and pray for them even if their sin is wronging you, and may you even offer them your love, which shames them and draws them to Christ.

5.25.0.en: The Jews asked Christ why His disciples did not fast, while the disciples of John and the Pharisees held to it. This was either a question of inquiry, or it shows their burden and complaint about fasting, or an objection against Christ and His disciples for their lack in this matter.

5.26.0.en: In His answer Christ gave a parable of the bridegroom and the wedding. As the people of the wedding rejoice in their bridegroom, so also Christ's disciples rejoice spiritually in beholding Him, but when the bridegroom is taken away the children of the bridechamber can fast. Likewise Christ's disciples, when He ascends to heaven, will feel their weakness and need, and will fast with asceticism and many prayers, and God will give them the knowledge of Him and the vision of Him spiritually. In application of this we keep the fast of the Apostles after the Ascension of Christ and the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit.

5.27.0.en: Then Christ addressed the problem of the Pharisees and lawyers who held to the letter of the Law without its essence, and how their spiritual practice is not acceptable as long as their heart is not pure. He made this clear by an example, which is mending an old garment by putting a new patch on it, for this does not benefit it but harms it, because the new piece's cloth is strong while the fabric of the old is weak, so it tears when the new patch is sewn into it, and the old garment becomes worse and more torn.

5.27.1.en: Likewise, if a person's life is not renewed by repentance and faith in Christ, his spiritual practices, prayers, fasts or any spiritual work do not benefit him.

5.28.0.en: Then He confirmed the same meaning as in the previous verse with a new example, which is putting new wine into old bottles. The bottle is a vessel in which wine is put, made of goatskin, and resembles a waterskin; and when wine is left for a time in the bottle it ferments and expands, so if the bottles are old they are dry and have lost their elasticity, and then they burst and are ruined, while the wine is spilled and poured out and lost. Therefore they put new wine into new bottles, which have the elasticity and expansion if the volume of the wine inside them increases.

5.28.1.en: So also the soul renewed in Christ in a spiritual life benefits from the spiritual practices and is in harmony with them.

5.28.2.en: Purify your heart by repentance and forgive others, and you will be able to enjoy your fasting and your prayers.

5.29.0.en: He confirms here also the difficulty of renewal and change for the soul that is accustomed to the material life, in moving to repentance from sin and fellowship with God, like one who tastes new wine and says the old is better, although the old wine has a high percentage of alcohol, but habit makes him hold to it though it has a strong effect on the body. Persevere in your striving to reject the beloved sin and the old life, and force yourself in spiritual striving until you become accustomed to it and enjoy it.

5.29.1.en: The call of the Apostles and the Sermon on the Mount
